standard_prerequisites.name: Morphisms of simplicial sets as compatible families of maps

core_obligations: Forward direction (proof lines 2945-2962): for f : U -> Delta[n] denote F : U_0 -> [n] the map u |-> f_u(0); then f_u(j) = F(eps^i_j(u)) for all j <= i, so f is completely determined by its restriction to sk_1 U (indeed to U_0).

Converse and the monotonicity reduction (lines 2962-2984): given F : U_0 -> [n] the rule f_u(j) = F(eps^i_j(u)) defines a morphism of simplicial sets exactly when all f_u are nondecreasing, which is equivalent to the inequalities F(eps^i_j(u)) <= F(eps^i_{j'}(u)) for j <= j'; since eps^i_j and eps^i_{j'} both factor through eps^i_{j,j'} : [1] -> [i], it suffices to check the inequalities for i = 1.
Conclusion (lines 2984-2986): Mor(U, Delta[n]) = Mor(sk_1 U, sk_1 Delta[n]) for every simplicial set U, so the canonical map is an isomorphism by the cosk_1 universal property.
proof_roadmap: Show a morphism into Delta[n] is determined by its degree-zero values.
Reconstruct the morphism from the degree-zero function and reduce monotonicity to degree one.
Conclude the bijection Mor(U, Delta[n]) = Mor(sk_1 U, sk_1 Delta[n]) and hence the isomorphism.
